The Government intends to award a contract resulting from this Request for Quotation (RFQ) to the responsible offeror whose quote conforms to the RFQ and represents the overall Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) to the Government, price and other factors considered. LPTA is determined by evaluating all non-cost proposals on an "acceptable vs. unacceptable" basis. Once a quotation meets the minimum objective standards deﬁned in the solicitation, the contract is awarded to the offeror with the lowest evaluated price, with no additional value given for exceeding technical requirements. To be eligible for award, the offeror must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at SAM.gov, have current representations and certiﬁcations, and not be listed on the SAM exclusions list. The Government will review each offeror's price and order them from lowest to highest priced. The Government will evaluate quotations in ascending price order until a minimum of two (2) quotations are determined to be Technically Acceptable. Under the LPTA approach, the Government will evaluate the three (3) lowest quotes up front if more than 3 offerors are received. This source selection will evaluate the lowest-price quote ﬁrst for technical acceptability, if it passes, the award will be made;

Effective air circulation in flight line facilities is critical for personnel safety, aircraft performance, and overall mission success. Since installation five years ago, the fans have not been serviced, increasing the risk of mechanical failure. An

n Antonio, Randolph Air Force Base (JBSA-Randolph) aircraft hangars. Effective air circulation in flight line facilities is critical for personnel safety, aircraft performance, and overall mission success. Since installation five years ago, the fans have not been serviced, increasing the risk of mechanical failure. An inoperable fan system poses a significant threat to both personnel (heat-related injuries) and sensitive aircraft components. This contract proactively maintains the integrity and safety of these vital hangar environments and mitigates the risks associated with equipment failure. 1.0 SCOPE. This PWS defines the requirements for a non-personal services to provide maintenance, repair, and installation at JBSA-Randolph. The contractor shall provide all supervision, labor, tools, materials, parts, transportation, and equipment (including all necessary lift equipment) to replace inoperable existing fans, perform annual preventative maintenance, diagnostics, and optional repairs for twenty-one (21) fans located across five (5) buildings. 1.1 Non-Personal Services. forms_signatures.text: . 1.0 SCOPE. This PWS defines the requirements for a non-personal services to provide maintenance, repair, and installation at JBSA-Randolph. The contractor shall provide all supervision, labor, tools, materials, parts, transportation, and equipment (including all necessary lift equipment) to replace inoperable existing fans, perform annual preventative maintenance, diagnostics, and optional repairs for twenty-one (21) fans located across five (5) buildings. 1.1 Non-Personal Services. The government will neither supervise contractor employees, nor control the methods the contractor performs the required tasks, nor prepare work schedules for individual contractor employees; however, the contractor shall consider the Government’s duty hours and work schedule. The Contractor shall perform annual preventive maintenance (PM) on all twenty-one (21) fans during each period of performance. To ensure standardized annual intervals, the Contractor shall execute the required PM event no earlier than four (4) months and no later than seven (7) months into the period of performance. The aptitudes and abilities measured by the ASVAB include General Science, Arithmetic Reasoning, Word Knowledge, Paragraph Comprehension, Mathematics Knowledge, Electronics Information, Auto Information, Shop Information, Mechanical Comprehension, and Assembling Objects. Test takers receive a standardized score from 1-100 for each of these subtests. The Army combines scores on the ASVAB subtests into composites, also known as aptitude areas (AAs) or line scores, to determine eligibility into each initial-entry MOS. For example, a Soldier would be eligible to enlist in the Fire Control Specialist MOS (13J) if they score an 83 on the Field Artillery composite AA that includes the subtests Arithmetic Reasoning, Mathematics Knowledge, and Mechanical Comprehension. There are currently 10 AA composites that are used to determine MOS eligibility: Clerical, Combat, Electronics, Field Artillery, General Maintenance, General Technical, Mechanical Maintenance, Operators and Food, Surveillance and Communications, and Skilled Technical. For example, a Soldier would be eligible to enlist in the Fire Control Specialist MOS (13J) if they score an 83 on the Field Artillery composite AA that includes the subtests Arithmetic Reasoning, Mathematics Knowledge, and Mechanical Comprehension. There are currently 10 AA composites that are used to determine MOS eligibility: Clerical, Combat, Electronics, Field Artillery, General Maintenance, General Technical, Mechanical Maintenance, Operators and Food, Surveillance and Communications, and Skilled Technical. Effective classification and assignment of Soldiers is dependent on being able to discriminate the different abilities of Soldiers based on how well they score on the AA composites of the ASVAB. The overarching objective of this effort is to conduct research to determine if the Army would benefit from updated AA composites used to determine MOS fit. The current project aims to identify potential redundancy within the current ASVAB AA composites,

The multi-domain operations (MDO) concept requires Army teams to operate semi-independently but also to utilize the capabilities across multiple domains to conduct sustained missions in highly contested environments. Additionally, high personnel turnover for teams is expected in the FOE as casualty counts increase, rapid teaming is required, and ad hoc teams become common. Teams must be capable of maintaining mission effectiveness despite this expected high personnel turnover. This research will identify the necessary combination of KSBs needing to remain on a team to ensure sufficient stability and mission effectiveness during team member trade-offs and will develop proofs of concept for a future Army capability to conduct focused, deliberate pre-deployment training for those KSBs. Within the literature, creativity has been conceptualized and examined as both an antecedent (e.g., Yang & Hung, 2021; Zhang & Bartol, 2010) and an outcome (e.g., Liu et al., 2022; Tierney & Farmer, 2011). In a recent review by Lua et al. (2024), the authors discuss creativity behaviors like idea implementation, innovative behavior, and personal initiative. Teng et al. (2020) examined the relationship between creative self-efficacy and innovative behavior. In the study, the authors used Scott and Bruce’s (1994) measure of innovative behaviors which includes items such as “generates creative ideas” and “develops adequate plans and schedules for the implementation of new ideas” (p. 607). For the purpose of this effort, we are interested in creativity as an outcome and, more specifically, creative performance with technology. Creativity research is not novel to the U.S. Army, but largely exists at the antecedent level. Two previous job analysis projects included innovation and creativity in surveys of talent requirements (Boyle et al., 2022) and personnel characteristics (Royston & Lin, 2022) across military occupational specialties (MOS). Additional ARI efforts have examined divergent thinking (Russell et al., 2017) and creative thinking (Zaccaro et al., 2012). Results for these reports indicate the importance of creativity across MOS and ranks but are not specific to creative performance behaviors with technology. 4 The purpose of this project is to develop and validate a measure of creative performance with technology. Measure items should capture individual-level indicators of creative performance that are relevant for Soldiers. This measure may capture a single domain or may involve multiple subscales. By assessing the underlying skills and abilities associated with success in Cyber work, the Army can identify high- potential candidates, meet the increasing demand for these personnel, more accurately predict performance, and reduce attrition during the training process. To aid in identification of high-potential candidates for Cyber training, the Army Research Institute (ARI) developed the Common Cyber Capabilities assessment (C^3).

term_value.text: upplemented with additional information included in this notice. Solicitation number 36C26126Q0750 is issued as a request for quote (RFQ). The Department of Veterans Affairs intends to award a service-based contract for landscape and grounds maintenance for the VA Central California Health Care Systems (VACCHCS). The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 561730, with a small business size standard of $9.5 Million. This acquisition is being conducted as a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business set-aside. The anticipated period of performance will consist of a base period with four (4) option years, as identified in the solicitation documents. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the current Federal Acquisition Circular. The full solicitation package, including the Performance Work Statement and attachments, is included with this posting. Offerors are responsible for monitoring this site for amendments or updates. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, which will be considered by the Government. Quotes shall be submitted in accordance with the instructions contained in the attached solicitation. An optional, but strongly encouraged, site visit will be held 5 August 2026

A este respecto, indicar que la dirección competente ha de regirse por un Sistema de Gestión de Calidad basado en la norma ISO 9000-2015, tal y como establece su Convenio Colectivo y que, naturalmente, se audita. Las actividades realizadas y el cumplimiento de la normativa descrita serán validados por la Dirección competente de la Agencia en materia de formación, comunicación y gestión del cambio.DEFINICIÓN DEL PLAN DE FORMACIÓNEl adjudicatario desarrollará un Plan de Formación atendiendo a los hitos establecidos en el Plan de Proyecto o en la ejecución de cualquiera de los servicios objeto del pliego, y deberá ser presentado a la Agencia con laantelación suficiente para que esté validado antes de que se inicie la fase de implantación. El Plan de Formación deberá inclui

vas.iv.Ámbito y Perfiles de Formación, distinguiendo entre:Usuarios de la Comunidad de Madrid, con sus diferentes perfilesEmpleados de la Agencia, con sus diferentes perfiles (mantenimiento legal, correctivo y evolutivo, soporte y atención a los usuarios, formadores, etc.)La formación se llevará a cabo, preferentemente en las instalaciones de la Agencia. No obstante, el adjudicatario tendrá que tener disponibilidad de las instalaciones que sean necesarias para el desarrollo de las acciones formativas planificadas, si así se lo requiere la Agencia.Dichas instalaciones deberán cumplir con la normativa relativa al Sistema de Gestión de Calidad (ISO 9001:2008),y así mismo, deberán estar ubicadas en una zona céntrica y bien comunicada de Madrid. Las instalaciones propuestas deberán tener todos los elementos necesarios para la impartición de las acciones formativas (fundamentalmente en lo que atañe a los equipos informáticos, instalaciones y mobiliario, accesibilidad y aspectos básicos de seguridad). Así mismo, si hiciese falta alguna conexión a las infraestructuras de la Agencia, éstas correrán a cargo del adjudicatario. La validación definitiva de las aulas, lahará la Agencia, de acuerdo con el estándar establecido.La formación dirigida a los diferentes perfiles deberá impartirse con el grad

umple con los objetivos de continuidad de negocio definidos en el proyecto Nexus.Transparencia para el usuario: Cambio entre CPDs sin interrupciones perceptibles.Gracias a la replicación activa y a los mecanismos de conmutación automática (failover), el traspaso de operaciones entre CPDs se realiza de forma imperceptible para los usuarios. Esto garantiza una Expdte.: ECON/000027/2026Página 261 de 329 experiencia fluida y sin degradación del rendimiento, incluso durante eventos críticos o mantenimientos programados.Seguridad reforzada: Cumplimiento de estándares internacionales.El Geocluster incorpora prácticas alineadas con normativas como ISO 27001 y NIST, asegurando la protección de datos y la resiliencia ante ciberataques. La redundancia y la sincronización constante contribuyen a minimizar riesgos asociados a pérdida de información o accesos no autorizados.Flexibilidad operativa: Mantenimientos sin impacto en la carga productiva.Al contar con servidores activos en más de un CPD, es posible realizar intervenciones técnicas, actualizaciones o pruebas en uno de los centros sin afectar la operación global. Esto optimiza la gestión de recursos, reduce ventanas de mantenimiento y mejora la eficiencia del equipo técnico.*** FIN DEL ANEXO 7 *** Expdte.: ECON/000027/2026Página 262 de 329 ANE

Factores operativos Continuidad del servicio: mantener la solución tecnológica basada en SAP garantiza el mantenimiento y evolución de este servicio público esencial que afecta a la gestión de ingresos, pagos, presupuesto, contabilidad, compras, logística y contratación de toda la Comunidad de Madrid. lizada a través de la Oficina de Proyecto y Producto, estructurada en torno a buenas prácticas SAP. Factores económicos Maximización de la inversión pública realizada durante más de 15 años en licencias, parametrización, desarrollos, integraciones y formación. Aprovechamiento de licencias y suscripciones adquiridas, cuyo coste ya ha sido asumido en expedientes recientes. Expdte.: ECON/000027/2026 Página 5 de 12 Evitar un coste muy elevado de sustitución, dado que cambiar de plataforma obligaría a reimplantar desde cero todos los procesos, suponiendo además incurrir en costes redundantes por duplicación de sistemas de gran complejidad y volumetría de gestión Prevención de sobrecostes normativos , ya que SAP incorpora actualizaciones estándar alineadas con normativa de contabilidad y contratación. La continuidad de NEXUS ECCL sobre tecnología SAP es la opción más eficiente, segura, sostenible y alineada con las inversiones realizadas y los requisitos del servicio público. Un cambio tecnológico supondría riesgos y sobrecostes injustificables, comprometiendo la operativa económico-financiera de la Comunidad de Madrid. ip_data_security.text: ncluding fixed-price incentive fee contracts. 1.2 Background The U.S. Army recognizes that investments in producibility and advanced manufacturing, as well as existing capabilities will need to continue to be made to support a vast array of cru- cial activities, including but not limited to acquisition, sustainment, logistics, and ultimately the Army’s Modernization of its Organic Industrial base (OIB). In order to deliver impactful operational results, the U.S. Army must modernize the OIB, particularly in the areas of agile / flexible facilities, connected digital enterprise, advanced manufacturing, Digital Twin, auto- mation, and cyber security. DEVCOM has coined these technologies collectively as Conver- gent Manufacturing. Additionally, Watervliet Arsenal is looking for modified existing commercial technologies, services, and concurrent manufacturing; in an effort to ensure no drop in capabilities and pro- ducibility. With the focus on both “new capabilities”, “modified existing capabilities”, and “opera- tional constructs” convergent manufacturing technologies will accelerate the OIB’s capability to get generalized and advanced solutions to the Warfighter while enhancing and optimizing the Defense Manufacturing Base for today and tomorrow’s missions. .204-7017 Prohibition on the Acquisition of Covered Defense Telecommunications Equipment or Services-Representation. 2021-05 PROHIBITION ON THE ACQUISITION OF COVERED DEFENSE TELECOMMUNICATIONS EQUIPMENT OR SERVICES-REPRESENTATION (MAY 2021) The Offeror is not required to complete the representation in this provision if the Offeror has represented in the provision at 252.204-7016, Covered Defense Telecommunications Equipment or Services-Representation, that it "does not provide covered defense telecommunications equipment or services as a part of its offered products or services to the Government in the performance of any contract, subcontract, or other contractual instrument." (a) Definitions. "Covered defense telecommunications equipment or services," "covered mission," "critical technology," and "substantial or essential component," as used in this provision, have the meanings given in the 252.204-7018 clause, Prohibition on the Acquisition of Covered Defense Telecommunications Equipment or Services, of this solicitation. (b) Prohibition. Section 1656 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018 (Pub. L. 115-91) prohibits agencies from procuring or obtaining, or extending or renewing a contract to procure or obtain, any equipment, system, or service to carry

OBJECTIVE IRS-CI is seeking a vendor that can provide a base year plus four option years Indefinite Delivery/Quantity contract to fulfil mandatory ammunition requirements. The equitable adjustment shall be based upon any increase or decrease in costs due solely to the variation above 115 percent or below 85 percent of the estimated quantity. These items are specifically limited to objects that were devoted to a traditional Native American religious ceremony or ritual and which have religious significance or function in the continued observance or renewal of such ceremony. "Objects of cultural patrimony" means Native American items having ongoing historical, traditional, or cultural importance central to the Native American tribe or Native Hawaiian organization itself, rather than property owned by an individual tribal or organization member. The Contractor shall obtain written approval from the COR prior to any work that will disturb or is likely to disturb identified or suspected ACM. If suspected, previously unidentified ACM is encountered, Contractor shall not disturb the material and shall block of area to prevent unauthorized access. If the material is friable or has been disturbed to the point that asbestos fibers may have been released, Contractor shall immediately seal off area, shut off air circulation, and take all other precautionary measures to ensure protection of personnel from asbestos hazards. Prior to an assessment, knowledge of the building systems and components present is necessary, since assessments are done against these components, not against the building as a whole. This information about the systems and components that make up a building is called the BUILDER Inventory. BUILDER has a vast library of predefined components which an assessor will select from, and the inventory collection process involves identifying the type, quantity, and year installed for all pertine nt components. These components are also organized into systems and sub-systems according to the UNIFORMAT classification hierarchy. When a specific instance of a component is recorded, this is called a component -section in BUILDER, and represents a single component assembly or collection of like components to be managed as a single unit. Q: Does the requirement mandate a 100% vendor-furnished rental model, or does SAVAHCS retain any existing Customer-Owned Linen Items (COLI) that the contractor will be required to process alongside rented inventory? A: A 100% vendor-furnished rental model. Q: If COLI processing is required, will the vendor be held liable for standard wear-and- tear or replacement costs for government-owned items? A: No. Q: What is the exact required Par level distribution across the health care system prior to Day 1 of contract performance (e.g., 3-Par, 4-Par, or 5-Par systemwide)? A: 3 Days. Q: What is the breakdown of initial Par stock required on-site at the SAVAHCS main campus versus off-site reserve? A: Off Site Reserve will be 96 hour contingency linen. Q: Will the VA provide an explicit physical technical specification sheet (e.g., thread count, GSM weight, fabric blend 55 / 45 cotton-poly vs. 100% barrier poly, color coding, surgical drape fluid-resistance ratings) for each line item? A: Fabric blend 55 / 45 cotton-poly vs. 100% barrier poly, color coding depending on the cost. 36C26227Q0001 Page 5 of 11 Q: Are micro-fiber mop heads, microfiber cloths, and barrier isolation gowns included in the general 1,350,000 lbs annual estimated volume, or are they counted / tracke

requirements, and designated delivery time slots for each satellite location. A: N/A. Q: Is the contractor required to supply all clean / soiled exchange carts, poly-dump carts, and wire delivery hampers? A: Contractor is required to supply all clean / soiled exchange carts. 36C26227Q0001 Page 6 of 11 Q: What are the physical dimensional constraints (height, width, depth) of the SAVAHCS logistics staging area, freight elevators, and clean linen rooms to ensure incoming contractor carts fit properly? A: Average dock dimensions for 24-foot box truck. Q: What is the minimum quantity of dedicated exchange carts required to remain on-site at SAVAHCS at all times? A: 30. Q: Is contractor performance restricted strictly to dock-to-dock exchange, or is the contractor responsible for internal ward-level replenishment / clean linen room stocking? A: Restricted strictly to dock-to-dock exchange. The Government intends to award a contract resulting from this Request for Quotation (RFQ) to the responsible offeror whose quote conforms to the RFQ and represents the overall Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) to the Government, price and other factors considered. LPTA is determined by evaluating all non-cost proposals on an "acceptable vs. unacceptable" basis. Once a quotation meets the minimum objective standards deﬁned in the solicitation, the contract is awarded to the offeror with the lowest evaluated price, with no additional value given for exceeding technical requirements. To be eligible for award, the offeror must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at SAM.gov, have current representations and certiﬁcations, and not be listed on the SAM exclusions list. The Government will review each offeror's price and order them from lowest to highest priced. The Government will evaluate quotations in ascending price order until a minimum of two (2) quotations are determined to be Technically Acceptable. Under the LPTA approach, the Government will evaluate the three (3) lowest quotes up front if more than 3 offerors are received. This source selection will evaluate the lowest-price quote ﬁrst for technical acceptability, if it passes, the award will be made;

Effective air circulation in flight line facilities is critical for personnel safety, aircraft performance, and overall mission success. Since installation five years ago, the fans have not been serviced, increasing the risk of mechanical failure. An

n Antonio, Randolph Air Force Base (JBSA-Randolph) aircraft hangars. Effective air circulation in flight line facilities is critical for personnel safety, aircraft performance, and overall mission success. Since installation five years ago, the fans have not been serviced, increasing the risk of mechanical failure. An inoperable fan system poses a significant threat to both personnel (heat-related injuries) and sensitive aircraft components. This contract proactively maintains the integrity and safety of these vital hangar environments and mitigates the risks associated with equipment failure. 1.0 SCOPE. This PWS defines the requirements for a non-personal services to provide maintenance, repair, and installation at JBSA-Randolph. The contractor shall provide all supervision, labor, tools, materials, parts, transportation, and equipment (including all necessary lift equipment) to replace inoperable existing fans, perform annual preventative maintenance, diagnostics, and optional repairs for twenty-one (21) fans located across five (5) buildings. 1.1 Non-Personal Services. forms_signatures.text: . 1.0 SCOPE. This PWS defines the requirements for a non-personal services to provide maintenance, repair, and installation at JBSA-Randolph. The contractor shall provide all supervision, labor, tools, materials, parts, transportation, and equipment (including all necessary lift equipment) to replace inoperable existing fans, perform annual preventative maintenance, diagnostics, and optional repairs for twenty-one (21) fans located across five (5) buildings. 1.1 Non-Personal Services. The government will neither supervise contractor employees, nor control the methods the contractor performs the required tasks, nor prepare work schedules for individual contractor employees; however, the contractor shall consider the Government’s duty hours and work schedule. If the contractor feels that any actions constitute or are perceived to constitute personal services, the contractor shall notify the Contractor Officer (CO) immediately. 2.0 APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS. The Contractor shall perform annual preventive maintenance (PM) on all twenty-one (21) fans during each period of performance. To ensure standardized annual intervals, the Contractor shall execute the required PM event no earlier than four (4) months and no later than seven (7) months into the period of performance. The aptitudes and abilities measured by the ASVAB include General Science, Arithmetic Reasoning, Word Knowledge, Paragraph Comprehension, Mathematics Knowledge, Electronics Information, Auto Information, Shop Information, Mechanical Comprehension, and Assembling Objects. Test takers receive a standardized score from 1-100 for each of these subtests. The Army combines scores on the ASVAB subtests into composites, also known as aptitude areas (AAs) or line scores, to determine eligibility into each initial-entry MOS. For example, a Soldier would be eligible to enlist in the Fire Control Specialist MOS (13J) if they score an 83 on the Field Artillery composite AA that includes the subtests Arithmetic Reasoning, Mathematics Knowledge, and Mechanical Comprehension. There are currently 10 AA composites that are used to determine MOS eligibility: Clerical, Combat, Electronics, Field Artillery, General Maintenance, General Technical, Mechanical Maintenance, Operators and Food, Surveillance and Communications, and Skilled Technical. For example, a Soldier would be eligible to enlist in the Fire Control Specialist MOS (13J) if they score an 83 on the Field Artillery composite AA that includes the subtests Arithmetic Reasoning, Mathematics Knowledge, and Mechanical Comprehension. The overarching objective of this effort is to conduct research to determine if the Army would benefit from updated AA composites used to determine MOS fit. The current project aims to identify potential redundancy within the current ASVAB AA composites,

The multi-domain operations (MDO) concept requires Army teams to operate semi-independently but also to utilize the capabilities across multiple domains to conduct sustained missions in highly contested environments. Additionally, high personnel turnover for teams is expected in the FOE as casualty counts increase, rapid teaming is required, and ad hoc teams become common. Teams must be capable of maintaining mission effectiveness despite this expected high personnel turnover. Within the literature, creativity has been conceptualized and examined as both an antecedent (e.g., Yang & Hung, 2021; Zhang & Bartol, 2010) and an outcome (e.g., Liu et al., 2022; Tierney & Farmer, 2011). In a recent review by Lua et al. (2024), the authors discuss creativity behaviors like idea implementation, innovative behavior, and personal initiative. Teng et al. (2020) examined the relationship between creative self-efficacy and innovative behavior. In the study, the authors used Scott and Bruce’s (1994) measure of innovative behaviors which includes items such as “generates creative ideas” and “develops adequate plans and schedules for the implementation of new ideas” (p. 607). For the purpose of this effort, we are interested in creativity as an outcome and, more specifically, creative performance with technology. Creativity research is not novel to the U.S. Army, but largely exists at the antecedent level. Two previous job analysis projects included innovation and creativity in surveys of talent requirements (Boyle et al., 2022) and personnel characteristics (Royston & Lin, 2022) across military occupational specialties (MOS). Additional ARI efforts have examined divergent thinking (Russell et al., 2017) and creative thinking (Zaccaro et al., 2012). Results for these reports indicate the importance of creativity across MOS and ranks but are not specific to creative performance behaviors with technology. 4 The purpose of this project is to develop and validate a measure of creative performance with technology. Measure items should capture individual-level indicators of creative performance that are relevant for Soldiers. This measure may capture a single domain or may involve multiple subscales. Cyber training for enlisted Soldiers is lengthy, challenging, and requires significant investment from the Army. The necessity of Cyber jobs has led to an increasing demand for quality personnel. By assessing the underlying skills and abilities associated with success in Cyber work, the Army can identify high- potential candidates, meet the increasing demand for these personnel, more accurately predict performance, and reduce attrition during the training process. To aid in identification of high-potential candidates for Cyber training, the Army Research Institute (ARI) developed the Common Cyber Capabilities assessment (C^3).

term_value.text: upplemented with additional information included in this notice. Solicitation number 36C26126Q0750 is issued as a request for quote (RFQ). The Department of Veterans Affairs intends to award a service-based contract for landscape and grounds maintenance for the VA Central California Health Care Systems (VACCHCS). The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 561730, with a small business size standard of $9.5 Million. This acquisition is being conducted as a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business set-aside. The anticipated period of performance will consist of a base period with four (4) option years, as identified in the solicitation documents. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the current Federal Acquisition Circular. The full solicitation package, including the Performance Work Statement and attachments, is included with this posting. Offerors are responsible for monitoring this site for amendments or updates. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, which will be considered by the Government. Quotes shall be submitted in accordance with the instructions contained in the attached solicitation. An optional, but strongly encouraged, site visit will be held 5 August 2026

A este respecto, indicar que la dirección competente ha de regirse por un Sistema de Gestión de Calidad basado en la norma ISO 9000-2015, tal y como establece su Convenio Colectivo y que, naturalmente, se audita. Las actividades realizadas y el cumplimiento de la normativa descrita serán validados por la Dirección competente de la Agencia en materia de formación, comunicación y gestión del cambio.DEFINICIÓN DEL PLAN DE FORMACIÓNEl adjudicatario desarrollará un Plan de Formación atendiendo a los hitos establecidos en el Plan de Proyecto o en la ejecución de cualquiera de los servicios objeto del pliego, y deberá ser presentado a la Agencia con laantelación suficiente para que esté validado antes de que se inicie la fase de implantación. El Plan de Formación deberá inclui

vas.iv.Ámbito y Perfiles de Formación, distinguiendo entre:Usuarios de la Comunidad de Madrid, con sus diferentes perfilesEmpleados de la Agencia, con sus diferentes perfiles (mantenimiento legal, correctivo y evolutivo, soporte y atención a los usuarios, formadores, etc.)La formación se llevará a cabo, preferentemente en las instalaciones de la Agencia. No obstante, el adjudicatario tendrá que tener disponibilidad de las instalaciones que sean necesarias para el desarrollo de las acciones formativas planificadas, si así se lo requiere la Agencia.Dichas instalaciones deberán cumplir con la normativa relativa al Sistema de Gestión de Calidad (ISO 9001:2008),y así mismo, deberán estar ubicadas en una zona céntrica y bien comunicada de Madrid. Las instalaciones propuestas deberán tener todos los elementos necesarios para la impartición de las acciones formativas (fundamentalmente en lo que atañe a los equipos informáticos, instalaciones y mobiliario, accesibilidad y aspectos básicos de seguridad). Así mismo, si hiciese falta alguna conexión a las infraestructuras de la Agencia, éstas correrán a cargo del adjudicatario. La validación definitiva de las aulas, lahará la Agencia, de acuerdo con el estándar establecido.La formación dirigida a los diferentes perfiles deberá impartirse con el grad

umple con los objetivos de continuidad de negocio definidos en el proyecto Nexus.Transparencia para el usuario: Cambio entre CPDs sin interrupciones perceptibles.Gracias a la replicación activa y a los mecanismos de conmutación automática (failover), el traspaso de operaciones entre CPDs se realiza de forma imperceptible para los usuarios. Esto garantiza una Expdte.: ECON/000027/2026Página 261 de 329 experiencia fluida y sin degradación del rendimiento, incluso durante eventos críticos o mantenimientos programados.Seguridad reforzada: Cumplimiento de estándares internacionales.El Geocluster incorpora prácticas alineadas con normativas como ISO 27001 y NIST, asegurando la protección de datos y la resiliencia ante ciberataques. La redundancia y la sincronización constante contribuyen a minimizar riesgos asociados a pérdida de información o accesos no autorizados.Flexibilidad operativa: Mantenimientos sin impacto en la carga productiva.Al contar con servidores activos en más de un CPD, es posible realizar intervenciones técnicas, actualizaciones o pruebas en uno de los centros sin afectar la operación global. Esto optimiza la gestión de recursos, reduce ventanas de mantenimiento y mejora la eficiencia del equipo técnico.*** FIN DEL ANEXO 7 *** Expdte.: ECON/000027/2026Página 262 de 329 ANE

Factores operativos Continuidad del servicio: mantener la solución tecnológica basada en SAP garantiza el mantenimiento y evolución de este servicio público esencial que afecta a la gestión de ingresos, pagos, presupuesto, contabilidad, compras, logística y contratación de toda la Comunidad de Madrid. lizada a través de la Oficina de Proyecto y Producto, estructurada en torno a buenas prácticas SAP. Factores económicos Maximización de la inversión pública realizada durante más de 15 años en licencias, parametrización, desarrollos, integraciones y formación. Aprovechamiento de licencias y suscripciones adquiridas, cuyo coste ya ha sido asumido en expedientes recientes. Expdte.: ECON/000027/2026 Página 5 de 12 Evitar un coste muy elevado de sustitución, dado que cambiar de plataforma obligaría a reimplantar desde cero todos los procesos, suponiendo además incurrir en costes redundantes por duplicación de sistemas de gran complejidad y volumetría de gestión Prevención de sobrecostes normativos , ya que SAP incorpora actualizaciones estándar alineadas con normativa de contabilidad y contratación. La continuidad de NEXUS ECCL sobre tecnología SAP es la opción más eficiente, segura, sostenible y alineada con las inversiones realizadas y los requisitos del servicio público. Un cambio tecnológico supondría riesgos y sobrecostes injustificables, comprometiendo la operativa económico-financiera de la Comunidad de Madrid. ip_data_security.text: ncluding fixed-price incentive fee contracts. 1.2 Background The U.S. Army recognizes that investments in producibility and advanced manufacturing, as well as existing capabilities will need to continue to be made to support a vast array of cru- cial activities, including but not limited to acquisition, sustainment, logistics, and ultimately the Army’s Modernization of its Organic Industrial base (OIB). In order to deliver impactful operational results, the U.S. Army must modernize the OIB, particularly in the areas of agile / flexible facilities, connected digital enterprise, advanced manufacturing, Digital Twin, auto- mation, and cyber security. DEVCOM has coined these technologies collectively as Conver- gent Manufacturing. Additionally, Watervliet Arsenal is looking for modified existing commercial technologies, services, and concurrent manufacturing; in an effort to ensure no drop in capabilities and pro- ducibility. With the focus on both “new capabilities”, “modified existing capabilities”, and “opera- tional constructs” convergent manufacturing technologies will accelerate the OIB’s capability to get generalized and advanced solutions to the Warfighter while enhancing and optimizing the Defense Manufacturing Base for today and tomorrow’s missions. .204-7017 Prohibition on the Acquisition of Covered Defense Telecommunications Equipment or Services-Representation. 2021-05 PROHIBITION ON THE ACQUISITION OF COVERED DEFENSE TELECOMMUNICATIONS EQUIPMENT OR SERVICES-REPRESENTATION (MAY 2021) The Offeror is not required to complete the representation in this provision if the Offeror has represented in the provision at 252.204-7016, Covered Defense Telecommunications Equipment or Services-Representation, that it "does not provide covered defense telecommunications equipment or services as a part of its offered products or services to the Government in the performance of any contract, subcontract, or other contractual instrument." (a) Definitions. "Covered defense telecommunications equipment or services," "covered mission," "critical technology," and "substantial or essential component," as used in this provision, have the meanings given in the 252.204-7018 clause, Prohibition on the Acquisition of Covered Defense Telecommunications Equipment or Services, of this solicitation. (b) Prohibition. Section 1656 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018 (Pub. L. 115-91) prohibits agencies from procuring or obtaining, or extending or renewing a contract to procure or obtain, any equipment, system, or service to carry

The second part will support technical assistance (TA) and capacity building to enhance e-government functionality. The TA will support integrating the databases of the three tax authorities and simplifying and automating business processes in seven large GoKP departments that together account fo

upport is critical to the success of the related interventions. OBJECTIVE IRS-CI is seeking a vendor that can provide a base year plus four option years Indefinite Delivery/Quantity contract to fulfil mandatory ammunition requirements. This request is for the acquisition of duty and training ammunition for IRS-CI’s Special Agents. The equitable adjustment shall be based upon any increase or decrease in costs due solely to the variation above 115 percent or below 85 percent of the estimated quantity. "Sacred objects" means Native American items that are specific ceremonial objects needed by traditional Native American religious leaders for the practice of traditional Native American religions by their present-day adherents. These items are specifically limited to objects that were devoted to a traditional Native American religious ceremony or ritual and which have religious significance or function in the continued observance or renewal of such ceremony. "Objects of cultural patrimony" means Native American items having ongoing historical, traditional, or cultural importance central to the Native American tribe or Native Hawaiian organization itself, rather than property owned by an individual tribal or organization member. The Contractor shall obtain written approval from the COR prior to any work that will disturb or is likely to disturb identified or suspected ACM. If suspected, previously unidentified ACM is encountered, Contractor shall not disturb the material and shall block of area to prevent unauthorized access. If the material is friable or has been disturbed to the point that asbestos fibers may have been released, Contractor shall immediately seal off area, shut off air circulation, and take all other precautionary measures to ensure protection of personnel from asbestos hazards. Prior to an assessment, knowledge of the building systems and components present is necessary, since assessments are done against these components, not against the building as a whole. This information about the systems and components that make up a building is called the BUILDER Inventory. BUILDER has a vast library of predefined components which an assessor will select from, and the inventory collection process involves identifying the type, quantity, and year installed for all pertine nt components. These components are also organized into systems and sub-systems according to the UNIFORMAT classification hierarchy. When a specific instance of a component is recorded, this is called a component -section in BUILDER, and represents a single component assembly or collection of like components to be managed as a single unit. Q: Does the requirement mandate a 100% vendor-furnished rental model, or does SAVAHCS retain any existing Customer-Owned Linen Items (COLI) that the contractor will be required to process alongside rented inventory? A: A 100% vendor-furnished rental model. Q: If COLI processing is required, will the vendor be held liable for standard wear-and- tear or replacement costs for government-owned items? A: No. Q: What is the exact required Par level distribution across the health care system prior to Day 1 of contract performance (e.g., 3-Par, 4-Par, or 5-Par systemwide)? A: 3 Days. Q: What is the breakdown of initial Par stock required on-site at the SAVAHCS main campus versus off-site reserve? A: Off Site Reserve will be 96 hour contingency linen. Q: Will the VA provide an explicit physical technical specification sheet (e.g., thread count, GSM weight, fabric blend 55 / 45 cotton-poly vs. 100% barrier poly, color coding, surgical drape fluid-resistance ratings) for each line item? A: Fabric blend 55 / 45 cotton-poly vs. 100% barrier poly, color coding depending on the cost. 36C26227Q0001 Page 5 of 11 Q: Are micro-fiber mop heads, microfiber cloths, and barrier isolation gowns included in the general 1,350,000 lbs annual estimated volume, or are they counted / tracke

requirements, and designated delivery time slots for each satellite location. A: N/A. Q: Is the contractor required to supply all clean / soiled exchange carts, poly-dump carts, and wire delivery hampers? A: Contractor is required to supply all clean / soiled exchange carts. 36C26227Q0001 Page 6 of 11 Q: What are the physical dimensional constraints (height, width, depth) of the SAVAHCS logistics staging area, freight elevators, and clean linen rooms to ensure incoming contractor carts fit properly? A: Average dock dimensions for 24-foot box truck. Q: What is the minimum quantity of dedicated exchange carts required to remain on-site at SAVAHCS at all times? A: 30. Q: Is contractor performance restricted strictly to dock-to-dock exchange, or is the contractor responsible for internal ward-level replenishment / clean linen room stocking? A: Restricted strictly to dock-to-dock exchange. evidence_quality_summary.rule: DOWNLOADED_PUBLIC is transport success only. Mandatory-gate review is permitted only when gate_readiness=true; publication notice PDFs are never promoted to DCE evidence.

review_contract: This file is only GPT Web work. BUSINESS_GATES rows have gate-ready DCE and narrowly-scoped deterministic physical rejects are removed before this boundary. DCE_AUTHENTICITY rows require GPT Web to verify retrieved candidate material first. Nothing in this inbox is a final verdict.
tick_contract: After GPT Web reviews a pass, add one durable reviewed tick per candidate to control/gpt_web_review_ledger.json. The next rebuild removes ticked rows automatically. A later DCE run may re-enter review.
final_bank_contract: Decided GREEN/YELLOW/RED/FINAL_SUPER_GREEN results belong in control/final_supergreen_bank.json, never mixed into this inbox.
pipeline_contract: harvest -> Qwen/local triage -> DCE/evidence -> deterministic post-DCE scope gate -> persistent GPT Web review inbox -> GPT Web review + tick -> final bank.
